summary: Stone birdcage light on Lighthouse Island at the mouth of Baileys Harbor, Door County: lit 1853, put out 1 Dec 1869, now a private, closed island.

lens.note: LighthouseFriends and WMHS give a sixth-order Fresnel, upgraded to fifth-order in 1858. The USLHS record gives the original optic as a reflector installed in 1853.

structures.note: Birdcage lantern. Limestone from Sweet's quarry (LighthouseFriends); the USLHS record gives rubblestone and a conical shape. 52 feet from ground to focal plane.

access.note: Privately owned. LighthouseFriends says grounds, dwelling and tower are closed. The USLHS record lists it as not open to the public.

facts.agency: Private owner (USLHS record; the island is privately owned per LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Lighthouse Island bought from Alexander Mitchell for $100 in November 1851 (LighthouseFriends); NRHP nomination says Sweet received federal approval for the light in 1851.
Construction began; materials carried to the island by wagon in a low-water year.
David Ward appointed first keeper on 10 February 1853.
Light went into operation at the opening of navigation.
USLHS gives an original optic of reflector type, installed 1853. LighthouseFriends and WMHS say sixth-order Fresnel. Disputed.
Fifth-order lens replaced the sixth-order (LighthouseFriends, WMHS).
Inspector for the Eleventh District found the light in 'very defective condition'; rebuilding required (LighthouseFriends).
Congress appropriated $15,000 to rebuild the station on 2 March 1867 (LighthouseFriends). WMHS dates the Board's Cana Island proposal to 1867; LighthouseFriends to later in 1867 or 1868.

On 20 July 1868 Congress authorized moving the light to Cana Island and appropriated $6,000 for the range lights (NRHP nomination). The light was not moved; it was discontinued in 1869 and the Cana Island light was a separate structure (Manitowoc Tribune, 1870).
Keeper William Darling extinguished the light for the last time on 1 December 1869, the last day of navigation that season.
USLHS record: discontinued 1870. The station's last light was extinguished on 1 December 1869 (LighthouseFriends, WMHS); the range lights and Cana Island light took over in early 1870.

notes_for_editor: NAME AND PLACE: the station is Baileys Harbor Light, the 'Bird Cage' light on Lighthouse Island (USLHS calls the location North Point Island). It is NOT the Baileys Harbor range lights (us-wi-baileys-harbor-range-front), which were built in 1869 and lit in 1870 and have their own record and story. Keep the two apart. The 1896-1897 Lighthouse Board and Life-Saving Service hits for 'Baileys Harbor' or 'Bailey Harbor' refer to the range lights or to the Baileys Harbor life-saving station (est. 1896) and are not used. DISAGREEMENTS, all stated in the story: (1) Original optic: USLHS says reflector, installed 1853; LighthouseFriends and WMHS say a sixth-order Fresnel, upgraded to fifth-order in 1858. (2) Tower material and shape: LighthouseFriends says limestone from Sweet's quarry; USLHS says rubblestone and conical. (3) End of service: LighthouseFriends and WMHS say the last light was 1 December 1869; the USLHS record gives discontinued 1870 (the story gives both). (4) Cana Island proposal: WMHS says the Board proposed it in 1867; NRHP gives the Act of 20 July 1868 (the story gives only the 1868 Act, through the NRHP). NOT FOUND: Lighthouse Board annual reports for 1853-1869 are not in the local corpus (the corpus starts in 1891 for the Board), so the 1866 inspection, the 1867 appropriation and the 1869 extinguishing rest on LighthouseFriends, which cites Keepers of the Lights (Karges, 2000), not read. A Manitowoc Pilot item of 16 December 1869 mentions the tug Kitty Snowe at Baileys Harbor after the scow Blue Bell went on the rocks 'in that vicinity'. It does not name the light, so it is not used. No storm, wreck or rescue is tied to this light in any source read, so the storms chapter is omitted. ROSTER: matched by roster.py to the light station (USLHS place baileys-harbor, Year Established 1853); the 7 lines match LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list; person slugs match roster.py --json. The roster lists David Ward twice (1853-1854 and 1854), with Albert Barry between; LighthouseFriends says Ward was replaced by Michael Green in September 1854. PRIVACY: William Darling's biography is printed by LighthouseFriends; it is kept to the service record and his public military service as printed. Alexander Mitchell (the seller of the island, 1851) is named as the source names him. The present private owner of the island is not named. ATMOSPHERE/EDITING: removed 'The lantern is what the light is remembered for' (no source), 'The mouth of the harbor was the problem' (framing), and 'badly decayed' (LighthouseFriends says 'advanced state of decay'). 'Door Peninsula' replaced by 'Door County' (WMHS). PHOTOS: the station record's Wikimedia postcard image was not checked for licence and is not added here. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited.
